title: Tenant-route uniqueness spine and hangover-windowing for low-latency Console queries
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem statement: Console frequently needs per-tenant counts of unique route invocations and active sessions for dashboards and SLA checks. Exact aggregation across billions of events is expensive and slow. Current ad-hoc approaches either over-count (session duplication) or scan large partitions causing high query tail latency and cost.

Goal: Design and implement a compact, query-friendly 'spine' table and a set of curated marts that support: (1) approximate unique route counts per tenant and time slice (HLL sketch materialization), (2) session hangover windowing to attribute invocations that straddle partition boundaries, and (3) low-latency denormalized slices for the Console UI and alerts.

Non-goals: We are not replacing archival raw event lakes or offline ML feature stores. This work focuses on nearline / daily materializations and query patterns serving Console UIs, billing-attribution jobs, and SLA monitors.
implementation_plan: 1) Schema design: create 'spine' table with one row per tenant/day/shard carrying HLL sketches for route-level uniqueness and summary aggregates (invocations, tokens, error_counts). Columns: tenant_id, day, shard_id, route_hll_base64, invocation_sum, token_sum, error_count, last_invocation_ts, hangover_flag. 2) Ingestion: incremental Spark job to ingest events and update HLL sketches using merge semantics; write to Iceberg with partitioning (day, tenant_hash_mod_128). 3) Hangover window: compute session-level sticky keys using session_id or fingerprint; when a session's first event falls in previous partition, mark hangover_flag and emit small compensating rows during daily compaction. 4) Materialized slices: build per-tenant per-route daily denorm view (materialized Iceberg table) using HLL_estimate(route_hll) and aggregated counts; generate pre-joined slices for the Console (last_7d, last_30d) refreshed hourly. 5) Query hints: add Presto/Trino optimizer hints and suggested predicates (tenant_id, day range) in the Console backend routes. 6) Migration: shadow-write for 2 weeks and run A/B comparison against existing exact counts on sample tenants. 7) Rollout: enable for low-volume tenants first, monitor quality/regression, then increase coverage.
acceptance_criteria:
- End-to-end pipeline produces daily spine rows for 95% of active tenants within 30 minutes of job completion.
- HLL-based route-unique estimates are within 2% of exact counts for tenants with >1k unique routes and within 5% for smaller tenants (empirical check on sample set).
- Console route-unique widgets query the denorm tables with 70% lower median latency and no more than a 10% increase in cost for the usage cluster.
- Hangover compensation reduces cross-partition duplication to <1% of total session-attributed invocations in tests.
- Migration runbooks and rollback paths documented with runbook link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/console-analytics/spine-hangover-runbook
notes:
Progress updates:
- 2026-02-25: Spike complete. Proved HLL merge and Base64 storage fits in Iceberg string column; memory usage for 128-shard merges is acceptable in Spark executors (tested on staging with 5M events).
- 2026-03-02: Data model review with PM and Design. Decided to keep per-shard granularity for parallel compaction; removed per-route HLL to avoid cardinality explosion (we store route-level HLLs only when route cardinality > threshold - fallback to exact deduping during compaction).
- 2026-03-08: PR opened for ingestion job: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console-analytics/pull/482. Waiting on infra review for new IAM role that allows Spark jobs to write to the curated Iceberg namespace.
- 2026-03-10: Observability: added metrics for HLL merge time, compaction duration, and hangover-correction counts to the Console Analytics dashboard: https://dashboard.redwood.ai/d/console-usage/spine-health (requires SSO).
review_feedback:
- PM (Ava Park): request explicit SLA for freshness for tenant-facing dashboards; added '30 minutes' freshness target.
- Data Infra (Liam O'Connor): suggested switching to 64-bit HLL sketch to reduce storage; marked as follow-up if we observe tail memory pressure.
- Security (Priya Nair): confirmed no PII in sketches; recommended adding KMS encryption at rest for the Iceberg tables (ticket created).
risks:
- HLL estimation may underperform for very small tenants (low cardinality). Mitigation: fallback to exact deduping in compaction for tenants with <1000 unique routes.
- Compaction job resource spikes when merging many shards. Mitigation: staggered compacts and adaptive executor scaling.
- Query correctness: slight discrepancies vs exact counts could confuse support teams. Mitigation: show 'estimate' label in UI and provide variance numbers.
